meta.source: U.S. Census Bureau, State Population Totals, Vintage 2025 (which states get a page); U.S. Energy Information Administration, 2020 Residential Energy Consumption Survey (RECS), Highlights for water heating in U.S. homes by state; state energy offices (rebate status)
meta.notes: One record per state cost page (/water-heater-installation-cost/{slug}/), the 10 most populous states by the Census Vintage 2025 estimate (POPESTIMATE2025). Other states stay unbuilt until Search Console shows these 10 index and rank (PHASES.md 6c). waterHeating = EIA RECS 2020, main water heating fuel, share of occupied homes; a share EIA withholds (Q) or has no sample for (N) is left out. rebate = the state's federally funded Home Energy Rebates appliance program (HEEHR, formerly HEAR) as its official page described it on rebate.checked; status is our one-word summary of that quote: open, limited, closed, notLaunched or unconfirmed (official page could not be opened from our checker). Review rebates every three months with data/incentives.json. Costs, prices and inlet temperatures are not stored here: they come from the shared cost model and the state data files (npm run build:data).

rebate.quote: As of August 31, 2026, HEEHRA rebates for Phase I are fully reserved.
rebate.summary: Phase I paid only for heat pump HVAC systems, not water heaters, and its money is fully reserved. Phase II has not been announced.

notes.heading: California requires earthquake straps
notes.text: California law requires every new and replacement water heater to be anchored or strapped so it cannot fall in an earthquake, and home sellers must certify that the water heater is braced. Budget for straps on any California replacement; in the calculator they are part of the code items extra.
notes.quote: New and replacement water heaters are required by law to be anchored or strapped to resist falling during earthquakes. Home sellers must certify to buyers that water heaters are braced.

rebate.program: Texas Home Energy Rebates (HOMES and HEARS)
rebate.quote: Current Status (Updated August 21, 2026) Rebates are not currently available.
rebate.summary: The programs are still being designed, and a launch date will be set once the state has DOE approval. SECO advises against signing anything tied to these rebates before they launch.

rebate.program: Florida Energy Saver Program (HOMES and HEEHR)
rebate.agency: Florida Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services, Office of Energy
rebate.quote: The High-Efficiency Electric Home Rebates (HEEHR) and Home Owner Managing Energy Savings (HOMES) programs are expected to launch in the future.
rebate.summary: Neither program takes applications yet. The portal lets you register for news on the timeline.

rebate.program: New York Home Energy Rebates (HER and HEAR)
rebate.summary: NYSERDA's rebate pages refused our checker on the check date, so we could not confirm what is open today. Ask NYSERDA or check the ENERGY STAR Rebate Finder before you count on a rebate.

rebate.quote: On June 1st, 2026, the Department of Energy released new program guidance. EPO is currently working to understand these changes, make the necessary changes to program design to be in compliance, and launch the program for consumers in the Commonwealth.
rebate.summary: The program is being redesigned after DOE's June 2026 guidance and is not open to homeowners yet.

rebate.quote: At this time, the Illinois EPA's IRA Section 50122 Home Electrification and Appliance Rebate Program, or HEAR Rebate Program, application has not yet been processed by USDOE or provided to Illinois EPA for administration or distribution.
rebate.summary: The appliance rebate has not launched. Illinois says it plans to give the first rebates to low-income households and will not pay rebates for work done before launch.

rebate.program: Ohio Home Energy Rebates (HOMES and HEEHR)
rebate.summary: We could not find a current status page from the Ohio Department of Development on the check date, and third-party trackers disagree. Ask the department or check the ENERGY STAR Rebate Finder before you count on a rebate.

rebate.program: Georgia's Home Energy Rebates (HER and HEAR)
rebate.quote: The HEAR program for single-family has reopened with limited measures.
rebate.summary: The reopened appliance rebate is limited to wiring and panel upgrades done with a whole-home efficiency (HER) project, so it does not pay for a heat pump water heater on its own.

rebate.program: Energy Saver North Carolina (HOMES and HEAR)
rebate.agency: NC Department of Environmental Quality, State Energy Office
rebate.quote: Up to $1,750 for an ENERGY STAR-certified electric heat pump water heater.
rebate.summary: The appliance rebate covers heat pump water heaters for households with income up to 150% of the area median, installed by a program contractor. Applications start at energysavernc.org.

rebate.program: Michigan Home Energy Rebates (MiHER: HER and HEAR)
rebate.quote: Governor Gretchen Whitmer announced the statewide launch of the Michigan Home Energy Rebates Program (MiHER)
rebate.summary: Michigan launched its rebates statewide in April 2025, including the appliance rebate for income-qualified homes. EGLE's own site refused our checker, so we could not confirm how much money is left today.
